page: Amazon Web Services r7a.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 192 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The memory subsystem consists of 1536.0 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. This instance utilizes the Nitro hypervisor and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps, but does not include local NVMe storage or hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is a primary strength, with both small-block cached and large-block uncached read operations achieving top-tier results. The system also demonstrates top-tier efficiency in software compilation, ray tracing, and Redis SET operations, which reached 323.08 million operations per second. However, single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression show average performance.

The hardware profile offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads, delivering high memory bandwidth and processing capacity without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPUs. A notable tradeoff is the weak text generation speed for small LLM models, which falls into the bottom 25%, though prompt processing speeds remain strong. This instance is suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching, software compilation, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
